deep_dive.executive_summary: Nucor is a best-in-class cyclical steel compounder with a vertically integrated EAF model and a heavy but largely funded growth capex wave. [Fact] FY2025 was strong: $7.52 diluted earnings per share, $3.23 billion operating cash flow, and moderate leverage (24.4% funded debt to capital). [Fact] Our proof-complete component schedule values one share at about $179 on a through-cycle base versus $231 today, implying about −3.5% per year over seven years. industry.structure: U.S. steel is concentrated among Nucor, Cleveland-Cliffs, U.S. Steel (now Cliffs-owned), and Steel Dynamics in flat and long products, with Nucor the largest EAF producer. Pricing follows global commodity spreads, scrap/DRI input costs, and import arbitrage; no single producer sets price.
industry.share_shift: EAF share of U.S. production continues to rise versus integrated blast-furnace capacity; Nucor gains on cost position and downstream integration (fabrication, rebar, joist, deck) while new domestic sheet capacity from multiple players increases supply-response risk.
industry.trend: Infrastructure and reshoring support domestic demand, but 2024–2026 brings a wave of new sheet and plate capacity, high startup costs, and volatile scrap/spread economics; AI/data-center and energy project demand partially offsets traditional construction cycles.
